failures.evidence:
`pi-legion` ended `failure` at the merge head 9dae22b73356 (check run 120396948671, run 39948484055, completed 2026-10-23T11:49:05Z), and the handoff commit 781ef78b was pushed above it. Its annotations name two failures in the repository's own skills guard, `packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts`, and both reproduce here:

  $ cd packages/pi-legion && bun test src/skills-guard.test.ts
  (fail) every staged file is under Oh My Pi's spill threshold, so a skill:// read arrives whole
    + { "bytes": 51617, "file": "legion-architect/SKILL.md" }
  (fail) every skill body stays under 500 lines, its detail in references
    + { "file": "legion-worker/SKILL.md", "lines": 501 }
  7 pass, 2 fail

The thresholds are `SPILL_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 50 * 1024` and 500 lines (packages/pi-shared/test/skills-guard.ts:14,124,134), both `>=`. The branch owns both crossings: on `main@origin` the two files are 499 lines and 50588 bytes, each under; at this branch's pre-merge head 4e229996 they were 499 lines and 49996 bytes, also under; at this head they are 501 lines and 51617 bytes. This issue is what grew them - the conditioned no-CI clause lengthened skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md, and the `merge-waiting` wake row lengthened skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md - and merging main consumed what margin was left. Neither file can be left over the line: Oh My Pi spills a file at or over the threshold, so `skill://legion-architect` stops arriving whole, which is the guard's whole subject.

No red test is needed and none was written: the repository's own suite already pins this, red, in one command, and the guard's message names the remedy it was written for - move the detail into references (skills/legion-worker/references/ and skills/legion-architect/references/ both exist and already carry this kind of detail).

Why nothing else would have caught it, which is why it is a failure and not a note: `pi-legion` is not in the base branch's required set (`gh api --paginate repos/sjawhar/legion/rules/branches/main` -> lint, typecheck, test, pr-title), so the daemon's checks-red scheduling never fires on it (classify judges only the required set), and this change deliberately removes READY's own read of the head's checks. A red lane the base does not require now reaches the merge unless a person or this phase reads it. That is the correct design and it is this issue's own: it makes reading CI at the head, which is this phase's job, the only thing standing between this red and main.

CI's remaining state at my last read, for the record rather than as part of the failure: `lint`, `typecheck` and `pr-title` success at that head; `test`, `dispatch`, `dispatch-memory`, `envoy-go`, `envoy-go-race` and `envoy-smoke` still `in_progress` after an hour of the merge's runs, so the required set is not yet settled either. I did not wait for them: the round fails on `pi-legion` whatever they come to, and the next round reads CI fresh at its own head.
